title: Simulated DOM Event Pipeline with Propagation Control
subtopicTitle: DOM Event Flow: Capturing, Bubbling & Delegation
concept: Event Phases (Capture -> Target -> Bubble) and Immediate Stop
problemStatement: Implement `dispatchTreeEvent(treeRoot, targetNode, eventName)` that simulates full DOM event flow: executes capture listeners down from root, target listeners on target, then bubble listeners back up to root. Supports `event.stopPropagation()` and `event.stopImmediatePropagation()`.
interviewTrap: Many engineers do not know the exact order: capture flows strictly root -> target parent, while bubbling flows target parent -> root.

testCases.name: Executes capture then bubble in correct sequence
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [() => {}], bubble: [() => {}] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [() => {}] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

testCases.name: stopPropagation prevents bubbling to parent
testCases.input: child stops propagation during target phase
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [() => {}], bubble: [() => {}] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [e => e.stopPropagation()] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

testCases.name: Capture phase stops immediately when stopped at root
testCases.input: root stops propagation during capture phase
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [e => e.stopPropagation()] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [() => {}] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Events travel down from `window` through the DOM tree (Capturing Phase) until they reach the target (Target Phase), then bubble back up to `window` (Bubbling Phase). Event delegation attaches a single listener to a common ancestor, querying `event.target.closest()`.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Event Phases (Capture -> Target -> Bubble) and Immediate Stop.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Event Phases (Capture -> Target -> Bubble) and Immediate Stop is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What are the three distinct phases of DOM event propagation?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) Capturing Phase: event trickles down from `Window` -> `Document` -> `<html>` -> `<body>` down to the target's parent. 2) Target Phase: event arrives at the target element. 3) Bubbling Phase: event bubbles back up from the target element back up to `Window`.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between event.stopPropagation() and event.stopImmediatePropagation()?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `stopPropagation()` prevents the event from traveling further up (or down) the DOM tree, but allows any OTHER event listeners registered on the CURRENT element to still execute. `stopImmediatePropagation()` stops tree propagation AND immediately blocks any remaining listeners on the CURRENT element from firing.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests precise understanding of propagation halting.

realWorldUseCases.description: Stopping click propagation on modal content boxes so clicking inside doesn't trigger backdrop close listeners.

howToExplain.opening: DOM event propagation follows a strict bidirectional pipeline: descending during the capture phase, reaching the target, and ascending during bubbling.
keyPoints: addEventListener third parameter `{ capture: true }` listens during capture phase.
stopPropagation halts tree traversal; stopImmediatePropagation also halts sibling listeners.
preventDefault cancels default browser actions (link navigation, form submit) without stopping propagation.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Mastering event phases allows surgical interception of user actions before child components receive them.
analogies: A scuba diver descending to the ocean floor (capture), touching the sunken treasure (target), and floating back to the surface (bubble).

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming stopPropagation() prevents the browser default action.
commonMistakes.why: stopPropagation only halts event traversal; it does NOT stop default actions like checkbox checking or link navigation.
commonMistakes.correct: Use e.preventDefault() to cancel default browser behaviors.

followUpDeepDive.question: What are Passive Event Listeners ({ passive: true }) and why do they improve scroll performance?
followUpDeepDive.answer: By passing `{ passive: true }`, the developer guarantees the listener will never call `e.preventDefault()`. This allows browser compositors to scroll the page immediately on the GPU thread without blocking to wait for the JavaScript thread to evaluate.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: W3C DOM Level 3 Events & Chrome Scrolling Performance
